title: [SPECFLOW] IMPROVE-CORE: verified single-cycle product improvement
body:
## Outcome

Ship a first-class `specflow improve --once` mode that can select one bounded product improvement, define what "better" means before implementation, use existing Specflow model-routing/build/verifier machinery, make the smallest useful change in an isolated workspace, and finish with an auditable `KEEP | REVERT | INCONCLUSIVE` decision.

(Full body: https://github.com/Hulupeep/Specflow/issues/171 — acceptance AC-CORE-1..8, snapshot 2026-09-26T12:37:01Z.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-CORE-1: `specflow improve --once` can start from an explicit product mission and current repository state, select one bounded candidate and record why it was selected.
- [ ] AC-CORE-2: No implementation starts until a frozen ImprovementContract defines the problem, user impact, hypothesis, baseline, acceptance, non-goals and evaluation method.
- [ ] AC-CORE-3: Product/UX candidates can remove friction or improve workflow without treating visual novelty or code churn as improvement.
- [ ] AC-CORE-4: Work happens in an isolated reversible git workspace; prohibited external side effects are blocked by default.
- [ ] AC-CORE-5: Existing Specflow routing/build/verifier/gate machinery is reused. A builder or provider self-review cannot establish success.
- [ ] AC-CORE-6: Every cycle terminates as KEEP, REVERT or INCONCLUSIVE, with predeclared acceptance and evidence strength preserved.
- [ ] AC-CORE-7: The ledger and report reconstruct candidate choice, contract, models, cost, implementation, evidence, decision and retained commit.
- [ ] AC-CORE-8: A real HeyStax/TabStax web-app run demonstrates one bounded product or subtle UX improvement with before/after evidence, explicit UX evaluation and no production side effects.
